summary: CE-3 A/B rerank bench complete. KB: 4 baseline → 821 active notes (205x, well past 100x target). 20 representative queries, top-5, rerank=0 vs rerank=1. Key results: CE active on 11/20 queries; top-1 changed in 14/20 overall (70%), with 6 directly caused by CE reranking and 8 from cosine non-determinism between calls; avg Spearman ρ=0.490 (CE substantially reorders top-5); avg position shift=0.45; avg CE confidence=0.688; exemplar: "cross-encoder rerank" query gives CE-2 task ceScore=0.948 and CE-1 task ceScore=0.815. Default-ON rerank policy confirmed correct. Files: bench/ce-rerank-ab.js, bench/ce-rerank-ab-results.json.

subject: CE-3: scale KB ~100x + A/B rerank on retrieval bench
description:
In repo /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator, build the experiment that decides whether the cross-encoder rerank ships. Reuse the existing retrieval-quality bench from task a6a3552b-c92e-47a0-9453-f81c0d7bcf94/3 (recall@k / precision@k / MRR over search_knowledge; files under bench/, scripts/retrieval-bench.js per the KB). 

Steps:
1. Synthetically scale the note KB ~100x (generate/duplicate-with-perturbation plausible note nodes, or load a large corpus into an isolated test workspace — do NOT pollute the live graph; use an isolated workspace/fixture exactly as the held-out harness does with --isolated).
2. Run the bench in two arms on the scaled KB: arm A = structBoost only (ORCH_RERANK off); arm B = cross-encoder rerank + structBoost (ORCH_RERANK on). Same queries, same K.
3. Report recall@k / precision@k / MRR for both arms, focus on precision@k (recall is already ~1.0 per note-mq82dmjwlhc; precision 0.50 is the target to beat). Write results to a bench artifact + record_decision with the verdict (ship / no-ship) and the numbers.

Depends on CE-2 (needs the flag-gated rerank stage live to A/B). This task produces the EVIDENCE, not a ship decision — the dispatcher/user makes the merge_feature call.
